title: Midnight at the Lumen Museum
brief: At the Lumen Museum gala, a planned ninety-second blackout began at 10:00 p.m. When the smart glass rebooted, Aurora Circuit—a kinetic light sculpture by the late Iris Venn—was gone. The secured wing was sealed immediately. Four people had relevant access, knowledge, or equipment: curator Mara Vale, lighting technician Theo Quinn, security lead Nia Brooks, and catalog photographer Rowan Pike.

suspects.name: Mara Vale
suspects.public_profile: Mara approved the catalog shoot, the display's calibration window, and a controller migration scheduled for the morning. Aurora Circuit anchors the museum's largest donor opening of the year.

suspects.name: Theo Quinn
suspects.public_profile: Theo built the gala lighting sequence and maintains the isolated booth. His contract ends after the exhibition opens, and the museum has not renewed it.

suspects.name: Nia Brooks
suspects.public_profile: Nia controls wing procedures, supervises equipment screening, and carries master access. She wrote the rule that all media cases must be weighed on entry and at locker intake.

suspects.name: Rowan Pike
suspects.public_profile: Rowan photographed Aurora Circuit before the gala and brought a hard equipment case into the wing. He previously documented Iris Venn's studio and helped organize her estate archive.

locations.name: Gallery 3
locations.description: The smart-glass display, its rear service panel, and the instrumented plinth.

locations.name: Media locker
locations.description: The secure room holding checked camera gear and removable media.

locations.name: Security screening
locations.description: The station that records incoming gear and locker-intake weights.

locations.name: Lighting booth
locations.description: The isolated room containing the cue console and legacy pulse controller.

observations.title: Plinth W-3 telemetry
observations.text: 9:39:04 p.m. — net load 1.84 kg. 9:42:18 p.m. — net load 0.00 kg. 10:00:00–10:01:30 p.m. — net load remains 0.00 kg. The post-incident sensor test passed.

observations.title: Rear-panel diagnostic
observations.text: During calibration mode, the hinge registered OPEN from 9:42:11 to 9:42:24 p.m. while the magnetic contact continued to report CLOSED. Inspectors recovered a small square of matte gaffer tape from the contact.

observations.title: Item recovered from the front guide
observations.text: A polarized acetate printed with Aurora Circuit's catalog image was wedged inside the smart-glass guide. It aligned convincingly from the brass viewing line but appeared flat after the glass rebooted.

observations.title: Gallery 3 access extract
observations.text: An occupancy sweep marked Gallery 3 empty at 9:37:40 p.m. Rowan entered at 9:39:04 under work order G3-CAT-17. No second entry was recorded before Rowan left at 9:45:11.

observations.title: Rowan's first statement
observations.text: “I stayed behind the brass line for the entire shoot. The closest I came was about three meters, and I never touched the display.”

observations.title: Camera frame RP_2207
observations.text: Captured at 9:42:14 p.m. In the polished edge of the display, Rowan's camera is reflected less than an arm's length from the case. The rear service panel is open beside it.

observations.title: Equipment-chain measurements
observations.text: Hard case RP-HC1: 7.92 kg at museum entry; 9.76 kg at media-locker intake. The equipment manifest is unchanged. Corridor footage records no handoff.

observations.title: BLACKOUT_90 console audit
observations.text: The cue was loaded at 4:10 p.m. and executed automatically at 10:00 p.m. No manual console input was recorded between 9:55 and 10:02.

observations.title: 9:42 synchronization snapshot
observations.text: Mara appears continuously on the greenroom feed. Theo appears inside the lighting booth. Nia's body camera records an uninterrupted loading-bay seal check. Gallery 3's access log lists Rowan.

observations.title: Commissioning note 14-B
observations.text: Scheduled for 7:00 a.m.: replace Aurora Circuit's original pulse controller. Legacy microtimings cannot be reproduced exactly after migration. Curator disposition: “Proceed. Visual variance is acceptable.”

observations.title: Catalog contact-sheet notation
observations.text: Three rehearsal frames mark the sculpture's irregular seventeen-second pulse with a double-ring symbol. The same symbol appears in the Iris Venn estate archive beside sequences cataloged as artist-timed. The sheet is signed “R. Pike — archival pass.”

observations.title: Production hold entry
observations.text: At 6:26 p.m., a forty-eight-hour estate technical review was entered against work order G3-CAT-17. Mara marked the request denied because the donor opening and 7:00 a.m. commissioning slot would not move.

observations.title: Mara's revised account
observations.text: Mara first calls the migration reversible. When shown note 14-B, she corrects herself: the old controller would remain only through morning verification and then be discarded. Exact preservation of Iris Venn's timing was not part of the donor deliverable.

observations.title: Theo's omitted warning
observations.text: Theo admits Rowan stood in the booth doorway when he warned Mara that no exact copy of the timing map existed. Rowan asked, “So once it is normalized, there is no way back?” Theo answered no. He hid the exchange because discussing conservation decisions could cost him his contract.

observations.title: Rowan and the Venn archive
observations.text: Mara confirms Rowan entered the hold attached to G3-CAT-17. He documented Iris's studio for six years and prepared much of the estate archive; he argued that her timing irregularities were deliberate. Mara knows of no financial dispute between Rowan and the museum.

observations.title: Climate-locker request
observations.text: Nia recalls Rowan requesting a climate-stable locker and asking whether an artist's estate could place a morning hold on checked equipment. She told him only the museum director or police could stop its release. Nia never opened the case.

observations.title: Rowan's changed account
observations.text: Confronted with frame RP_2207, Rowan says he crossed the brass line only to correct glare at Mara's request. Mara denies giving that instruction, and work order G3-CAT-17 contains no close-access task.

observations.title: Manifest reconciliation
observations.text: Rowan says a second battery pack explains the later weight. Nia's entry manifest lists that battery inside RP-HC1 before the first weighing, and no additional pack appears at screening. Rowan maintained control of the case until locker intake.

timeline_events.summary: Rowan asks Mara for a forty-eight-hour estate review; she declines.
Rowan is the only recorded occupant of Gallery 3.
The plinth's 1.84-kilogram load falls to zero.
Rowan's hard case moves from entry screening to the media locker under his control.
The preloaded blackout runs automatically; the smart glass reboots clear.
The original pulse controller is scheduled to be replaced after morning verification.

reveal_routes.summary: The display case records establish when the plinth changed and how the empty display was masked.
The screening desk aligns Gallery 3 access with the two equipment-case measurements.
The console audit shows whether the blackout required a person at the controls.
Synchronizing access and camera records isolates who was in Gallery 3 when the plinth changed.
Mara's first answer changes when the commissioning note is placed in front of her.
Theo admits someone outside the technical team heard exactly what the migration would erase.
Mara describes a connection to Iris Venn that predates the museum commission.
The security desk log gives Nia's account of Rowan's unusual locker request.
Rowan changes his story when confronted with the reflected service panel.
The entry manifest, two weighings, and chain of custody test Rowan's battery explanation.
